subject: Draft MAP: Integration & SDK build plan for PulseX - milestone owners + target close
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Petrova <anya@pulsex.health>, Marcus Reed <m.reed@pulsex.health>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Draft MAP: Integration & SDK build plan for PulseX - milestone owners + target close

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. As promised, attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan focused on the integration build milestone. This email summarizes the MAP items for the SDK/streaming/tool-calling milestone and proposes owners, dependencies, and a target close so we can align on next steps.

Attachment: MAP_PulseX_v1.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
Attachment: integration_specs.xlsx (XLSX, 420KB)

Key milestone: Integration build (phase 1) — scope
- SDK integration (JavaScript + Python): embed Redwood client, auth flow, sample snippets
- Streaming output: SSE or WebSocket support for partial token streaming
- Tool calling: one outbound tool (FHIR lookup) via authenticated REST call + webhook handler
- Structured outputs: JSON schema for the clinical summary and trace metadata (v1)

Proposed owners and rough ETA (target close for this milestone: 2027-01-15):
- Integration spec & SDK samples: Tessa Morgan (SE) — dev spike complete by 2026-12-08
- Backend integration & tool-calling adaptor: Dev Patel (Engineering) — initial integration by 2026-12-22
- Security checklist & audit artifacts: Laura Bennett (Security) — review by 2026-12-29
- Customer rollout & validation: Monica Patel (CS) + PulseX technical lead — validation window 2027-01-03 -> 2027-01-12

Dependencies and risks:
- Procurement: signed SOW + Data Processing Addendum (DPA) — blocking for any staging credentials
- Network: PulseX must expose webhook endpoint for tool callbacks (or allow Redwood IPs)
- Data schema: mapping from PulseX FHIR subset to Redwood structured-output schema (linked in spreadsheet)

Ask from you (short):
1) Confirm Marcus as your technical owner for the build / integration testing.
2) Flag any internal procurement timelines that could shift the target close.
3) Any showstopper constraints on webhooks or client SDK installation.

I'll update the MAP with any feedback and ship a version with explicit task-level estimates by 2026-11-23. If useful, we can slot a 30-minute technical sync next week (Dev + SE + PulseX devs).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189
[Attachment: MAP_PulseX_v1.pdf]

From: Anya Petrova <anya@pulsex.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Reed <m.reed@pulsex.health>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Integration & SDK build plan for PulseX - milestone owners + target close

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear breakdown and attachments. Quick notes from PulseX side:

- Yes, Marcus will be the technical owner for integration (cc'd). He'll own webhook setup and internal dev testing.
- Procurement: our legal ops has a vendor review queue and has given us an estimated 3-week lead time for standard SOW + DPA. That likely moves the credential/staging access until early December.
- For streaming, our preferred approach is WebSocket (we have an existing gateway). SSE would be a fallback.

A couple of asks to include in the MAP:
- Can Redwood provide a sample Python SDK install that works inside our container images (Debian 12)?
- For tool calling (FHIR lookup), can you document the authentication modes supported for callbacks (Bearer token vs mTLS)? We may prefer mTLS for production.

I'll run the attachments by our dev team and loop back with any redlines. Proposed internal milestone adjustment: if procurement takes 3 weeks, target close for the integration milestone could shift to 2027-01-31. Can you confirm if Redwood can compress any of the implementation windows?

—Anya
Director, Integrations | PulseX Health
anya@pulsex.health | +1 617-555-0294

[Inline: Marcus (cc) — please confirm if the WebSocket gateway is available for a dev subdomain before Dec 8.]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T01:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Integration & SDK build plan for PulseX - milestone owners + target close

Adding some technical estimates and callouts so we can set expectations with PulseX. Numbers are rough; I can convert to story points if you prefer.

Implementation plan (phase 1) — dev notes:
- SDK samples (JS + Py) — 3 dev days + 1 day SE review. Target internal PRs by 2026-12-05. Deliverables: quickstart repo, container-friendly wheel, example auth snippet (API key + OAuth flow). Owner: Tessa to draft samples, I'll review.
- Streaming support (WebSocket primary): ~4 dev days to wire up the WS transport on top of our streaming infra + 1 day to add client-side sample. Requires a dev staging host that accepts persistent WS connections. Owner: Dev Patel.
- Tool calling adaptor (FHIR lookup): 6 dev days to implement adaptor + retry/circuit logic + a small connector to accept Bearer token or mTLS. Important: mTLS will need cert exchange; add 2 days for cert-handling docs. Owner: Dev Patel.
- Structured output schema: 2 days to finalize v1 schema and add validation; SE will include mapping examples to PulseX FHIR subset. Owner: Tessa Morgan.

Total engineering effort (parallelizable): ~16 dev days across 2 engineers. If PulseX can provide staging access and webhook endpoint as soon as procurement is cleared, we can maintain the original schedule. If procurement slips to early December (3-week timeline), pushing the milestone to 2027-01-31 is reasonable unless we run an overlapping fast-track (Redwood SE + 1 eng) — that could close by 2027-01-15 but with reduced validation window.

Security notes for Laura:
- We'll prepare the security checklist and SOC artifacts; need to confirm whether PulseX requires an IP allowlist or full VPC peering.

Next technical step I recommend: 60-minute sync (Dev + Tessa + Marcus) to confirm webhook format, auth method (mTLS vs bearer), and streaming choices. Proposed slots: 2026-11-24 10:00-11:00 PT or 2026-11-25 09:00-10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: integration_specs.xlsx]

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Integration & SDK build plan for PulseX - milestone owners + target close

Great — thanks everyone for the quick responses and the helpful detail, Anya and Marcus. Summary of agreed updates and next steps (I will push an updated MAP v1.1 by COB 2026-11-23):

1) Confirmed owners
- PulseX technical lead: Marcus Reed
- Redwood SE: Tessa Morgan (samples + mapping)
- Redwood Eng lead: Dev Patel (adaptor + streaming)
- Security: Laura Bennett
- CS validation: Monica Patel

2) Timeline options
- Baseline: target close 2027-01-15 (if procurement + staging access in early Dec)
- Contingency: target close 2027-01-31 (if procurement takes full 3-week queue)
- Fast-track option: Redwood can compress to 2027-01-15 with a smaller validation window if PulseX can supply staging webhook/wss by 2026-12-08.

3) Immediate asks for PulseX
- Marcus: confirm dev subdomain for WebSocket by 2026-12-01 (or provide schedule).
- Anya: confirm procurement milestone dates so we can lock a deployment window.

4) Next meeting: propose 60-min technical sync with Marcus, Dev, Tessa — 2026-11-24 10:00 PT (or 11/25 morning as backup). Monica will join for rollout planning.

I will also seed DocuSign for the SOW placeholders (you'll get a link next week once legal ops greenlights the MSA/DPA template).

Thanks — I'll send v1.1 with explicit task-level estimates and an updated gantt in the shared Drive.

Best,
